_about: Numbers cited by the robot-stack-contention kit. Every value is 'public' (URL), 'sibling' (a key in a sibling kit) or 'illustrative' (a round teaching number that keeps the shape of a finding, never a measurement). No number here is a measurement. Load this file; do not retype the numbers.

board_cores.source: illustrative: a 12-core embedded SoC (Orin-class); 8 shared, 4 reserved

pool_cores.source: illustrative: shared pool of general-purpose cores

reserved_cores.source: illustrative: cores reserved (isolated) for pinned real-time and robot services

stack_services.source: illustrative: a full robot stack with every module on; a freshly booted robot runs fewer

pool_busy_frac_full.source: illustrative: shared pool about four fifths busy in the full stack

pool_wait_per_busy_full.unit: s of run-queue wait per busy s

pool_wait_per_busy_camera_only.source: illustrative: almost no queueing with one module

saturated_core_equal_share.source: illustrative: three groups on one saturated core each get about a third

detector_frame_ms_solo_full.source: illustrative: object detector frame time alone vs full stack

detector_added_wait_run_blocked.source: illustrative: most of the full-stack rise is CPU (wait + slower run)

detector_vla_added_blocked_wait_run.source: illustrative: next to the VLA the rise is mostly blocked (GPU) time

instr_growth.source: illustrative: user instructions per work unit unchanged

cycles_growth_range.source: illustrative: the same instructions take 1.4-2x the cycles

ipc_drop_range.source: illustrative: instructions per cycle fall by a third to a half

l3_refill_ratio_range.source: illustrative: more L3 refills per instruction (a hint, not a cause)

cluster_move_recovered.source: illustrative: moving cluster neighbours away recovers about two thirds, on a pre-registered class line

cluster_move_camera_cost_hz.source: illustrative: the move overloads the shared pool and costs the camera frames

weight_wait_per_cpu_s.source: illustrative: the camera's own CPU wait falls by about three quarters

weight_camera_hz.source: illustrative: the camera recovers part of its rate, not all of 30 Hz

weight_others_wait_rise.source: illustrative: other services wait longer: the wait moves

ms_per_history_item.source: illustrative: one log line per history item on the event loop

history_items.source: illustrative: conversation history that is not reset

context_build_ms_filtered.source: illustrative: the same step with the per-item lines dropped

transcript_latency_ms.source: illustrative: most of the rise was the logging loop

interaction_accepted_ms.source: illustrative: about 90 % of the rise was our own probe

probe_cores_wanted.source: illustrative: a topic probe subscribed to heavy streams

probe_on_pool_camera_cost_hz.source: illustrative: moving the probe to the shared pool costs the camera frames

probe_receive_delay_ms.source: illustrative: the probe's own receive delay on a saturated core

mps_no_concurrency_quote.value: Work launched to the compute engine from work queues belonging to different CUDA contexts cannot execute concurrently.

timeslice_ms.source: illustrative: a GPU time slice per context is a few milliseconds (driver default, priority dependent)

dose_curve_points.unit: [other share O points, added blocked ms per frame]
dose_curve_points.source: illustrative: convex: each point costs more near saturation

dose_vla_point.source: illustrative: the VLA sits on the compute co-tenant's curve

dose_slopes.source: illustrative: slopes grow along the curve

dram_null_added_ms.source: illustrative: a memory-copy co-tenant with the same GPU time adds nothing

burst_length_effect_ms.source: illustrative: 3 ms vs 30 ms bursts at the same share cost the same

camera_hz_alone.source: illustrative: the depth camera service's frame rate when it runs alone

camera_gpu_only_loss_hz.source: illustrative: GPU load alone (idle CPU) costs the camera no frames

camera_pool_loss_hz.source: illustrative: camera loss rises steeply with CPU wait

camera_fanout_loss_hz.source: illustrative: extra topic subscribers make the camera do more work

camera_full_stack_loss_hz.source: illustrative: 30 -> 25 Hz in the full stack

kernel_time_sms_full_share.source: illustrative: about half the kernel time leaves the SMs >= 90 % full on some resource (theoretical)

gemm_warp_slot_fill.source: illustrative: big GEMM kernels fill SMs by registers while using few warp slots

multiwave_share.source: illustrative: kernels larger than one wave of the GPU

sm_issue_full_stack.source: illustrative: low issue rate while the GPU is busy

gpu_active_full_stack.source: illustrative: GPU has work about 60 % of the time

mps_tegra_unsupported.value: -multiuser-server; GPU compute modes; under MPS: CUDA IPC, cooperative launches, client termination

mps_launch_path_quote.value: MPS clients submit work directly to the GPU without passing through the MPS server.

mps_one_user.value: the control daemon runs one server per Linux user at a time; other users' clients are queued

mps_probe_busy_frac.source: illustrative: two one-SM test clients: turns vs side by side

mps_cap_visible_sms.source: illustrative: a 25 % thread cap leaves 4 of 16 SMs

launch_overhead_us.source: illustrative: per-launch cost is the same with and without MPS

shape_rate_fraction.source: illustrative: GEMMs at a model's own shapes reach well below the ceiling

vision_encoder.source: illustrative: a ViT-class encoder with high weight-side intensity

vision_pred_bandwidth_form_ms.source: illustrative: weights / bandwidth: too fast on a compute-bound board

vision_measured_ms_orin.source: illustrative: a measured-style Orin vision-phase time inside the compute-form bracket

vision_compute_form_ms.source: illustrative: FLOPs / shape rate = 0.5 TFLOP / (42.5 TFLOP/s x 0.6 .. 0.4)

gpu_processes_full_stack.source: illustrative: processes holding GPU memory in the full stack

vla_gpu_ms_per_call.source: illustrative: GPU work inside one call (the rest is CPU side)

gpu_free_next_to_stack.source: illustrative: GPU time left next to the full stack

sharing_overhead.source: illustrative: each output costs this much more GPU time when shared

batch1_latency_ms.source: illustrative: one observation -> one action chunk, batch 1
